title: Rearranging Fruits
summary: You have two baskets, each containing n fruits, with the cost of each fruit specified in the arrays basket1 and basket2.
statement: You have two baskets, each containing n fruits, with the cost of each fruit specified in the arrays basket1 and basket2. You can perform a swap operation between the i -th fruit of basket1 and the j -th fruit of basket2, with the cost of the swap being the minimum of the two fruit costs. The objective is to make both baskets identical by sorting them, and you need to find the minimum total cost to achieve this. If it is impossible to make the baskets identical, return -1.
constraints: The two baskets have equal size; one swap exchanges one fruit across baskets.
A swap costs the smaller of its two fruit values.
Return minimum cost to make sorted baskets identical, or -1 if impossible.
hints: Combined fruit counts must be even; each basket needs half of every value.
Collect the absolute half-surpluses from both baskets and sort them.
Only the smaller half determines direct swap costs; each can instead travel through the global minimum for cost twice that minimum.
Pairing smallest surplus values with largest opposite values minimizes direct costs, while the minimum-fruit detour caps every pair independently.
editorial: Pairing smallest surplus values with largest opposite values minimizes direct costs, while the minimum-fruit detour caps every pair independently.
